page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, relying instead on remote Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in compute-heavy and instruction-extended workloads. The server achieved a Passmark CPU score of 66066.16 and a database operations score of 22291.38, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.1 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scored 303.78 GB/sec. In memory-bound tests, the instance demonstrated a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 3532.24 GB/sec, though uncached large block write bandwidth dropped to 68.56 GB/sec. Redis SET operations performed strongly at 79.02 million operations per second. For machine learning workloads, prompt processing for a 7B LLM model reached 243.16 tokens per second, though text generation on larger 70B models was limited to 2.92 tokens per second.

The D48ls_v7 offers a specialized hardware profile that trades memory capacity for high-frequency compute power. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and no local storage, it is designed for workloads where CPU throughput is the primary constraint rather than memory footprint or local disk I/O. This resource density provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks, avoiding the expense of unutilized memory. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, cryptographic processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
